title: The road to U.S. citizenship
sub: The 10 official steps, from green card to citizen
source: Steps from USCIS, “10 Steps to Naturalization”. Not legal advice.

steps.t: Determine if you are already a U.S. citizen
steps.d: Some people are already citizens through a parent. If that is not you, go to the next step.

steps.t: Determine if you are eligible to become a U.S. citizen
steps.d: Usually 5 years as a permanent resident, or 3 if you are married to and living with a U.S. citizen.
Read the instructions and collect your documents, such as travel dates, addresses, jobs and tax transcripts.
steps.k: Keep a copy for your interview

steps.t: Submit your Form N-400 and pay your fees
steps.d: File online or on paper. USCIS sends you a receipt notice.

steps.t: Go to your biometrics appointment, if applicable
steps.d: If USCIS needs your fingerprints and photo, it sends you an appointment notice.
An officer goes through your application under oath and gives you the English and civics tests. Bring your appointment notice.

steps.t: Receive a decision from USCIS on your Form N-400
steps.d: Granted, continued or denied. Continued means USCIS needs more documents, or you retake a test 60 to 90 days later.

steps.t: Receive a notice to take the Oath of Allegiance
steps.d: The ceremony may be on the same day as your interview. If not, USCIS mails you a notice.

steps.t: Take the Oath of Allegiance to the United States
steps.d: Hand in your green card, take the oath, and receive your Certificate of Naturalization. You are not a citizen until you take the oath.
Learn your rights and responsibilities as a citizen. Then apply for a passport, register to vote, and update your Social Security record.
